newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers put off plans to ban tobacco ads.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers put off plans to ban tobacco ads.

text.p: European Union health ministers, abandoning for now efforts to prohibit all tobacco advertising, agreed a text on Tuesday that simply urges EU countries to continue to coordinate their anti-smoking efforts.
The text, adopted one day before the European Commission is to debate the future of EU tobacco subsidies, also asks the Commission to consider how the EU could support the initiatives.

At the insistence of Greece, one of the top recipients of EU tobacco subsidies, the ministers deleted a phrase asking the Commission to take into account the detrimental effects of smoking when considering tobacco-related policies, EU officials said.

EU Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn said he planned to highlight in Wednesday's Commission debate the contradiction between EU support for tobacco growing and its campaign to reduce smoking-related cancer deaths.
He also confirmed that he plans to propose on November 27 new EU measures to discourage tobacco consumption that will be based heavily on recommendations made by an EU group of cancer experts.
They recommended lowering the nicotine content of cigarettes, banning additives other than tobacco unless they are proven to be non-toxic and strengthening health warnings on tobacco products.

EU ministers have been deadlocked for years over a proposal to extend the EU's ban on television advertising of tobacco products to cover all advertising. Ireland, the current EU president, decided to shelve it until the political climate changes.

But Flynn told the news conference he had no plans to withdraw the proposal. EU officials say the tide could turn if Britain's Labour Party wins the national election which must be called by late May.
Labour is expected to reverse Britain's opposition to the proposal, which could allow it to go through.

Flynn has drawn up a paper proposing that the EU phase out its tobacco production aid. But he could have trouble winning support from the full Commission on Wednesday since the proposal would face political opposition from the EU's eight tobacco- growing countries, headed by Italy and Greece. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
